name: Off Highway Recreational Vehicle
description: Any mechanically propelled vehicle the rider sits on, used for recreation on rubber tires or tracks over unimproved terrain; a dirt e-moto is a trail bike, one class of OHRV, and a pedaled bike with a motor outside the e-bike limits is an OHRV too. Registered with Fish and Game.

restrictions.rule: A trail bike is any motor-driven wheeled vehicle with a seat or saddle designed or adapted for travel off maintained roads
No limit on motor power or speed; electric bicycles are excluded
Registered with Fish and Game each year, unless ridden only on land its owner owns or leases; no one under 18 may register one
Off the owner's or family's land, riders 12 or older need an OHRV or snowmobile training certificate or a driver's license, and riders under 14 must be accompanied by a qualified adult 18 or older
Riders under 18, and passengers under 18, must wear a helmet meeting FMVSS 218
Every rider needs eye protection unless a windshield protects their eyes and face
Ridden on someone else's land only with written permission, or on trails designated for wheeled OHRVs

On the traveled portion of a public highway, only where permitted, by a licensed driver or a trained rider 12 or older accompanied by a licensed driver 25 or older; never directly across an interstate, divided highway or toll road
Not above 4,000 feet except on designated roads and trails
